canonical_project: AVAIO Digital Leo / Little Rock AI-ready data-center and power campus
aliases: AVAIO Digital Leo / Little Rock AI-ready data-center and power campus
AVAIO Little Rock AI-ready data-center and power campus

location.address_or_area: 145th Street, Little Rock, Pulaski County, AR

status_as_of_cutoff: Announced / local process. AEDC and Entergy confirm the project announcement and utility-service context; AVAIO's current owner page reports a fully approved site plan, broken ground, 150 MW initial grid capacity online in 2027, and a broader 1.07 GW baseload path. Pulaski County records reviewed in this refresh show active moratorium/regulatory proceedings, but no county-published site-plan approval, building permit, construction inspection, CO, or actual energization record was located.

actions.government_body: Arkansas Economic Development Commission / State of Arkansas
actions.result_status: AEDC announced AVAIO Digital Leo near Little Rock in Pulaski County, with an initial 150 MW Entergy contract, anticipated growth to 1 GW, a 760-acre site, and a forecast of first-phase construction and June 2027 energization.
actions.access_caveat: AEDC announcement is a state/company economic-development record and does not substitute for local land-use or building approval.
actions.evidence_note: The announced 150 MW contract and future 1 GW expectation are not treated as energized load.

actions.government_body: Entergy Arkansas / Little Rock regional public partners
actions.result_status: Entergy reported that regional partners launched a fact-information site for proposed Little Rock-area data centers; the page identifies AVAIO as a Pulaski County project but is not a service agreement, permit, or local approval.
actions.access_caveat: Utility customer information is not an interconnection order or proof of construction.
actions.evidence_note: Utility identification is recorded separately from zoning, building, environmental, and occupancy actions.

actions.government_body: Pulaski County Quorum Court Agenda Committee
actions.result_status: County minutes record competing proposed twelve-month moratorium ordinances for high-intensity digital infrastructure / high-impact utility-intensive industrial uses. Item 26-I-45A failed to receive a do-pass recommendation; Item 26-I-52 received an 8-1-1 do-pass recommendation, with one justice stating the item would not protect residents from the AVAIO data center.
actions.vote_tally: 26-I-45A do-pass failed 6-3-1 present; 26-I-52 do-pass passed 8-1-1 present
actions.access_caveat: Committee minutes concern countywide regulation/moratorium items, not an AVAIO site-plan approval or building permit.
actions.evidence_note: Supports 'local process' status and public regulatory scrutiny; does not establish construction or energization.

actions.result_status: KATV reported that the Quorum Court voted down a proposed one-year data-center moratorium, leaving Pulaski County without an active moratorium and allowing AVAIO's proposed first phase near Wrightsville to continue moving through development process while county leaders consider permanent standards.
actions.access_caveat: Local media report used for full Quorum Court outcome because the official full-meeting minutes were not located in the public county page during this refresh.
actions.evidence_note: Treats the project as not paused by a county moratorium, but still not independently verified as permitted or under construction by a county permit record.

actions.government_body: Pulaski County Quorum Court Agenda Committee
actions.result_status: County agenda lists Item 26-I-56, an ordinance to regulate high-intensity digital infrastructure uses in unincorporated Pulaski County, classify them as heavy industrial, and establish conditional-use permitting, performance standards, cost recovery, inspection, monitoring, enforcement, decommissioning, and other safeguards.
actions.access_caveat: Agenda item is scheduled for consideration and is not a final adopted ordinance in the reviewed record.
actions.evidence_note: Confirms continuing local regulatory process as of the refresh date.

actions.result_status: AVAIO's current Leo page identifies the site as 145th Street, Little Rock, Pulaski County, AR at 34.623375, -92.246825; states 760 acres; reports 1,070 MW total baseload power, 570 MW grid power, 500 MW behind-the-meter baseload power, 75+ MW planned solar, broken ground, a fully approved Site Plan, an executed Entergy ESA for initial grid capacity energized in April 2027, and further 420 MW Entergy grid power planned for 2030.
actions.access_caveat: Owner/developer page is not a county permit, inspection, or energization record; the claimed site-plan approval and ground-breaking need official local-government corroboration.
actions.evidence_note: Capacity values are treated as contracted/planned/owner-reported, not energized load.

capacity_mw.evidence_note: Owner-reported and planned/contracted capacity; no energized-load record found.

sources.match_reason: Exact Phase3↔regional stable-ID pair; seed merged only with explicit evidence

contradictions.issue: Owner page reports broken ground and a fully approved Site Plan, while the refresh did not locate a public Pulaski County site-plan approval, building permit, inspection, certificate of occupancy, or energization record; local media still describes AVAIO's first phase as moving through development process.

Capacity framing differs by source: AEDC's January announcement says 150 MW contracted and up to 1 GW anticipated, while AVAIO's current project page states 1,070 MW total baseload power, 570 MW grid power, 500 MW behind-the-meter baseload, and 75+ MW planned solar.
